subject: gk
question: In the context of India's trade policies between 1947 and 1990, what was a common characteristic of the approach towards imports?

options.text: Promoting imports as a way to boost domestic competition.
Primarily focusing on the import of luxury goods and consumer durables.
Following a strategy of import substitution to protect domestic industries.
Encouraging unrestricted import of all goods.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Following a strategy of import substitution to protect domestic industries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India adopted a policy of **import substitution** between 1947 and 1990 to promote self-reliance and reduce dependency on foreign goods.
 
• Import substitution focused on **restricting imports of manufactured goods** and encouraging domestic production through tariffs and quotas.
 
• The strategy aimed to **protect nascent domestic industries** from international competition and foster industrial growth.
 
• Heavy industries and public sector enterprises were given priority under this policy to create a robust infrastructure for self-sufficiency.
 
• This approach was aligned with India's broader **planned economic development** strategy, as outlined in the Five-Year Plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI)**:

 
 
• ISI is an economic policy that advocates replacing foreign imports with domestic production.
 
• It aims to reduce foreign dependency and encourage local industries to grow.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Trade Policy (1947-1990):**
 
 
• India's trade policies during this period were influenced by the socialist model of economic planning.
 
• High import tariffs and quantitative restrictions were imposed on foreign goods.
 
• Exports were promoted selectively to generate foreign exchange.
 
 
 
• **Role of Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans provided a framework for import substitution by emphasizing industrialization and self-reliance.
 
• Sectors like steel, cement, and heavy machinery were prioritized for domestic production.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Import Substitution:**
 
 
• While it helped develop domestic industries, import substitution led to inefficiencies due to lack of competition.
 
• It also resulted in a limited choice of goods for consumers and technological stagnation in certain sectors.
